data.description:
New Workspace sheet (Sources/CreateWorkspaceSheet.swift): make the recent-directory picker the fast path. Atin's words: "a really core part of the workflow... bump it up a notch."

DESIGN IS PENDING ATIN'S PROTOTYPE FEEDBACK. Do not start until this line is replaced by "Prototype approved".
Prototype (real recents, local only, never commit it to this public repo): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-atin-Projects-Stage11-code-overwatch/fd4968b2-46ae-44b9-bfb9-e30b29645592/scratchpad/prototype.html

Root causes found
1. Auto-center on click. selectRecent sets keyboardSelectedRecentIdx; recentsList's onChange then runs proxy.scrollTo(id, anchor: .center) on every change, clicks included.
2. Double-click is already wired (TapGesture count 2 + simultaneous count 1), but the first click recenters the list, so the second click lands on whatever row slid under the cursor. Fixing 1 is most of the fix for 2. Verify that a double-click creates the workspace for the row that was clicked, with the list scrolled to its middle.
3. The recents list caps at 50 (CreateWorkspaceRecents.maxCount) and is full today. save() keeps prefix(maxCount) of an unsorted list, so the cap can evict a pinned entry or a recent one instead of the oldest.

Spec (subject to prototype feedback)
- A click selects and fills the path field; it never scrolls. Keyboard ↑↓ scrolls only enough to keep the selection visible (no .center anchor; nil or nearest behavior).
- Double-click on a recent row or a pin chip creates the workspace immediately with the selected layout.
- Pins move out of the list into a horizontal row of chips above it (★ name, a ⌘1–⌘9 badge, × on hover in the badge's slot so the width holds, drag to reorder, empty state "Star a recent directory to pin it here"). Pinned dirs are not repeated in the list except in search results. Pin order is user order: persist it (e.g. a pinnedOrder field or a separate key). Migrate existing pins.
- ⌘1–⌘9 creates a workspace from pin N.
- A search field sits above the list beside the sort control. It has focus when the sheet opens, and typing anywhere outside a text field goes to it. The field shows "N of M". Matching: a subsequence within the directory name scores highest (prefix and word-boundary bonuses); elsewhere in the path only a contiguous substring counts. Results rank by score, and the sort control is disabled while a query is active. The top hit is auto-selected so ⏎ opens it. ↑↓ move the selection while focus stays in the search field. Esc clears a non-empty query; Esc on an empty query cancels the sheet as today. Matched characters are highlighted in gold. There is an explicit no-match state.
- Denser rows: one line, 28 pt: name (13 medium), parent path (11 mono, dim, truncated), relative time (fixed width, tabular), ×count (fixed width), and a pin star in a reserved slot so nothing shifts on hover. About 12 rows are visible where about 6 are today. The sheet grows to about 1030 pt, so on a short screen the list, not the sheet, must give up height.
- Evict the oldest unpinned entry at the cap and never a pinned one; raise maxCount (proposal: 200) now that search makes a long tail useful.
- Footer hint: "Click selects · double-click or ⏎ creates · ↑↓ move · ⌘1–⌘9 open a pin".

Acceptance
- Unit tests for the recents model: eviction never drops a pin, pin order persists and migrates, fuzzy ranking on a fixed fixture.
- Real-app validation through the c11-computer-use skill on a tagged Debug build: click a row mid-list (no scroll), double-click (creates that row's dir), ⌘N then type then ⏎, ⌘2, pin/unpin/reorder, the no-match state, a short window.
- Localized strings go through String(localized:) as today.

Prototype (the visual and behavioral reference; it holds Atin's real paths, so read it in place and never copy it into this public repo): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-atin-Projects-Stage11-code-overwatch/fd4968b2-46ae-44b9-bfb9-e30b29645592/scratchpad/prototype.html (logic in prototype.src.html beside it). The dashed "Prototype controls" panel is not part of the design.

Root causes found
1. Auto-center on click: selectRecent sets keyboardSelectedRecentIdx, and recentsList's onChange runs proxy.scrollTo(id, anchor: .center) on every change, clicks included.
2. Double-click is wired, but the first click recenters the list, so the second click lands on a different row.
3. Recents cap at 50 (full today); save() keeps prefix(maxCount) of an unsorted list, so the cap can evict a pinned or recent entry.

Spec
- A click selects and fills the path field; it never scrolls. Only ↑↓ scroll, from handleArrow, with scrollTo(id, anchor: nil); never from onChange. Selection is stored as a path, not an index (the index goes stale when a filter, sort or pin changes the order).
- Double-click on a row or tile creates the workspace immediately with the selected layout. Ignore a double-click that arrives within about 400 ms of a pin change (a click on ★ or × changes the layout under the cursor).
- Pins: rectangular tiles about 120 × 86 pt above the list. A gold ★ sits top-left and a ⌘N badge top-right (× on hover in the same slot, so nothing shifts). The name is centered with the parent folders under it at about 60% white. No monogram. Tiles fill row by row: five in a row, then a second row; past two full rows the grid keeps two rows and scrolls horizontally. Drag reorders them. The empty state reads "Star a recent directory to pin it here". Double-click creates.
- Pinned directories also appear in the recents list in their normal sorted position (not floated to the top), with a gold star.
- Long names (tiles): choose the rendering with a pure, unit-tested function that measures seam segments with NSString.size(withAttributes:). A seam is after - _ . or at a camelCase or letter-digit boundary. The name wraps only at seams, never mid-word, in two lines at most; if that doesn't fit, it drops to 11.5 pt; if one unbreakable segment still doesn't fit, it goes on one line with a middle ellipsis ("Superca…docious"). Do not rely on Text lineLimit + minimumScaleFactor: SwiftUI breaks an over-long word between characters. The parent line shows the last two folders and drops to one ("…/greenwood-tech") before truncating the tail. The tooltip always has the full path.
- ⌘1–⌘9 creates from pin N immediately. MUST: today the app-level shortcut monitor treats ⌘digit as selectTab (AppDelegate ~11436); the modal guard (~10894) never trips because this is a window, not a sheet. In handleCustomShortcut, return false when event.window === createWorkspaceSheetWindow. Verify in the real app.
- Search sits above the list beside the sort control. It has focus on open, and typing outside a text field goes to it. It shows "N of M". A subsequence within the directory name scores highest (prefix and word-boundary bonuses); elsewhere in the path only a contiguous substring counts. Results rank by score, the sort control is disabled during a query, and the top hit is auto-selected so ⏎ opens it. Matched characters are highlighted in gold. Implement it as an NSSearchField representable whose control(_:textView:doCommandBy:) handles moveUp/moveDown (move the selection), insertNewline (create; ⌥ switches, see below) and cancelOperation (clear a non-empty query, otherwise close). Drop the container's .focusable() and onKeyPress arrows. The Cancel button's .cancelAction must not swallow Esc while a query is non-empty. With no matches, clear the selection and disable Create so ⏎ never creates in a stale directory.
- Already-open indicator: rows and tiles whose directory already has a workspace open in this c11 show a small green dot. Every row reserves the dot slot so names stay aligned. Double-click and ⏎ still create a new workspace (Atin's rule); ⌥ double-click and ⌥⏎ switch to the existing workspace and close the window. Match on the workspace root directory, standardized.
- Missing directories: stat off the main thread (a hung network mount must not stall the UI) and cache per open of the sheet. A missing directory shows struck through and dimmed, with "missing" in the time column. Double-click or ⏎ on it does not create; it flashes the row and explains.
- Right-click on a row or tile opens a menu: New workspace here (⏎), Switch to open workspace (⌥⏎, disabled unless open), Pin/Unpin, Reveal in Finder, Copy path, Remove from recents. Remove also drops the pin.
- Rows: one line, 28 pt: name (13 medium), parent path (11 mono, raise to about 0.5 opacity for contrast), relative time (fixed width, tabular), ×count (fixed width, fits 4 digits), and a pin star in a reserved slot.
- Workspace name: one line, label left, field right, the default name as placeholder; the hint moves to a tooltip.
- Layout cards: about 96 pt squares with the letter-cell icon and label; the description moves to the tooltip.
- Height: compute the list's row count (8 to 16) from the target screen's visibleFrame before layout. Every other section keeps its size; below 8 rows the content scrolls. Keep the list height fixed across states (one or two pin rows, no-match state) so the window never resizes mid-use. When it does resize, pin the window's top edge.
- Data: keep pins in a separate ordered key (createWorkspace.pins.v1: [String]). Keep writing the per-entry pinned flag so older builds read it. Migrate existing pins in their current display order. Normalize paths in record() (standardize, strip a trailing slash). The recents cap is 250; at the cap, evict the oldest unpinned entry, never a pin. Never let a decode failure return [] and then save over history: fail soft and keep the stored data.
- Accessibility: rows and tiles get .accessibilityElement(children: .combine), the .isButton trait, and an "Open" action; pin buttons are labeled "Pin <name>".
- Footer hint: "Click selects · double-click or ⏎ creates · ↑↓ move · ⌘1–⌘9 open a pin".

Acceptance
- Unit tests: eviction at 250 never drops a pin; pin order persists; migration from a real v2 blob keeps every entry and pin; path normalization; fuzzy ranking; the long-name layout function on fixed fixtures.
- Real-app validation (c11-computer-use skill, a tagged Debug build): click a row mid-list (no scroll); double-click it (creates that row's directory); ⌘N, type, ⏎; ⌘2 with another workspace open (creates, does not switch tabs); pin, unpin, reorder; 12+ pins (horizontal scroll); long names; Esc with a query (clears) and without (closes); ⌥⏎ on an open directory (switches); a missing directory; right-click menu; a short screen.
- Localized strings go through String(localized:).

Phase 2, same PR (folded in from C11-241 and C11-242 at Atin's request: expand a ticket's scope rather than file new ones). Land and validate phase 1 first, then:

Path mode in search: when the query starts with ~ or /, search switches from filtering to a path. The first row is "Create in <path>" for the typed path, followed by directories under it (real filesystem children listed off the main thread, plus known recents). Tab completes the highlighted child; ⏎ creates in the typed or highlighted path even if it is not a recent; a nonexistent path shows the missing state and does not create. The prototype mocks this (type ~/Projects/).

CLI and socket for recents and pins, sharing the sheet's model and ranking:
- c11 workspace recents list [--json] [--pinned]: path, lastOpenedAt, openCount, pinned, pin index, open-in-c11 and exists flags.
- c11 workspace recents pin|unpin|remove <path>; pin --at <n> sets the pin order.
- c11 workspace new --dir <path-or-fuzzy-query> [--layout <blueprint id>] [--name <n>]: resolves a fuzzy query with the sheet's ranking (fails loudly and lists candidates when the top two tie) and records the open in recents like the sheet does.
- An open sheet updates live when an agent changes pins.
- Document it in skills/c11/references/api.md and sync the installed skill per CLAUDE.md.
Phase 2 acceptance: unit tests for path-mode resolution and CLI query resolution; the real app with path mode (complete, create, missing); and each CLI verb run against the tagged build's socket with the sheet open.

Merged as PR #457 (squash 711faff24), 2026-09-30, with Atin's explicit approval.

Review trail:
- Design: three HTML prototype rounds with Atin, plus a fresh-context design review (11 findings, folded into the spec before the build).
- Build: Sonnet worker, phases 1 and 2 in one PR (C11-241 and C11-242 folded in at Atin's request).
- Code: fresh-context review of the PR found 14 issues (1 must, 8 should, 4 nits, test gaps); all fixed. 68 picker unit tests pass.
- Atin's own click-through of the tagged build: pinning, double-click, keyboard shortcuts and search all work. Two changes followed: the name column hugs its width (path gets the rest), and the picker shows only the four standard layouts (custom blueprints stay CLI-only).
- Merged with origin/main (8 commits, bonsplit bump); the Debug build succeeds locally, and all CI checks pass on the merge head.

Not verified on screen: the final column-width change (built, not relaunched, so Atin's screen stayed free); window re-sizing when the picker moves to another display; VoiceOver labels.
